block.paragraph: Design basis: LRFD 10th Edition (2024) ; FDOT Structures Manual, January 2026. RFQ V6.0 Addendum 5 — Governing Regulations controls the contract edition and Task Work Order exceptions.

textcell.paragraph: Objective
Determine global superstructure uplift, bearing reactions and pier load transfer.
Inputs
C001 wind; C002 fence load; live bridge geometry and classified permanent loads.
Output
Concurrent bearing reactions, contact/stability checks and signed pier load sets.

block.paragraph: Strength III minimum-gravity combinations; both transverse wind directions are tabulated in the bearing check.
Pier applicability: only the Strength III perpendicular-wind/uplift case is evaluated here. Service IV is not used for the current nonprestressed pier / steel-pile configuration.
The source wind geometry is provisional. Positive reactions establish contact for this load model only; pad compression, rotation, shear and connection capacities are separate checks.
1. Model, sign convention and live inputs.
• Read geometry from the project sources, define positive compression, and locate both the bearing plane and the cap reference.
2. Gravity classification and load combinations.
• Separate above-bearing gravity from substructure weight, then apply the existing minimum-gravity factors for each limit state.
3. Concurrent wind and bearing equilibrium.
• Combine C001 vertical wind with matching horizontal wind and resolve the windward-quarter-point eccentricity into unequal beam reactions.
4. Individual bearing reactions and restraint.
• Apply each span contribution to its physical bearings, reverse wind direction, and evaluate contact, overturning and restraint demand.
5. Pier load transfer for FB-MultiPier.
• Collect the physical bearing rows at the pier nodes and retain only the residual couples not already carried by the transferred forces.
6. Coherence, equilibrium and release checks.
• Reconcile geometry, weight classification and force/moment equilibrium; retain the live bearing-datum release condition.

textcell.paragraph: SOLUTION APPROACH

textcell.name: UpliftOverview2
textcell.paragraph: • C001 supplies vertical wind and the matching perpendicular concrete wind. C002 supplies the existing fence load. Geometry and weights remain live project references.

textcell.name: UpliftOverview3
textcell.paragraph: • Resolve concurrent vertical force and transverse overturning at each span end into individual beam-bearing reactions. Sum span contributions only after checking each physical bearing.

textcell.name: UpliftOverview4
textcell.paragraph: • Report contact, overturning, and hold-down demand; provide a separate pier load transfer with explicit residual moments.

MODEL ASSUMPTIONS

textcell.name: UpliftAssumptions2
textcell.paragraph: • T is transverse, L runs from End Bent 1 toward End Bent 2, and V is upward; axes are right-handed. B− and B+ are at negative and positive transverse coordinates. Reactions are positive in compression.

textcell.name: UpliftAssumptions3
textcell.paragraph: • The deck and diaphragms distribute global transverse overturning to the beam lines. Girders are simply supported for vertical load; deck continuity at the pier does not impose girder flexural continuity.

textcell.name: UpliftAssumptions4
textcell.paragraph: • Uniform equivalent loads use the project span and tributary-length definitions. Equal transverse DC/DW distribution, level bearing reaction planes and common end-section geometry are adopted. Local thickened-end weight is not credited.

textcell.name: UpliftAssumptions5
textcell.paragraph: • C004 uses the explicitly perpendicular horizontal case from LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1 . C002’s simplified transverse/longitudinal combination remains a separate load case; do not merge its independent components into these rows.

DERIVED EQUILIBRIUM

textcell.name: UpliftEquilibriumBasis2
textcell.paragraph: • For either simple-span end, multiply each line-load reaction by the adjacent span tributary length. Reverse the transverse wind sign to swap windward and leeward beam reactions.

textcell.name: UpliftEquilibriumBasis3
textcell.paragraph: • The force and moment formulas below are static equilibrium, not separate LRFD equations. Each case retains simultaneous gravity, upward wind, horizontal wind and eccentricity.

block.paragraph: Span 1 rows apply at End Bent 1 and the back-span bearing row at the pier. Span 2 rows apply at the ahead-span pier row and End Bent 2. Each row gives the reactions of individual physical bearings, not paired pier nodes.

*Horizontal demand assumes equal transverse shear sharing by the beam bearings and the same simple-span distribution as C002. Final restraint stiffness and load path must support that distribution; no pad or connection shear capacity is asserted.

textcell.paragraph: BEARING RESTRAINT BASIS

textcell.name: UpliftRestraintScope2
textcell.paragraph: • The bearing contact model carries compression only and credits no tensile resistance. A negative reaction is a required hold-down force, not force that an unanchored pad can transmit.

textcell.name: UpliftRestraintScope3
textcell.paragraph: • FDOT SDG 6.5.F /H requires approval for uplift and uplift restraints. Rebalancing gravity or revising the structural arrangement precedes restraint design.

textcell.name: UpliftRestraintScope4
textcell.paragraph: • FDOT SDG 6.5.3 requires the lateral restraint load path to be established. Concrete shear lugs for concrete-beam bridges are restricted to the specified extreme-event use; they are not credited for these wind cases.

textcell.name: UpliftRestraintScope5
textcell.paragraph: • Bearing-pad and anchorage capacities are not defined in these calculations. Contact results do not establish pad shear, compression, rotation, anchorage, diaphragm or foundation adequacy.

COMPLETE CONCURRENT PIER LOAD SET — APPLY ONCE

textcell.name: UpliftFBMPRules2
textcell.paragraph: • Use the factored downward node loads below at transverse coordinates minus and plus half the beam spacing, at the pier centerline and cap-reference elevation. They replace the corresponding DC/DW-plus-wind vertical totals; they are not additional gravity loads.

textcell.name: UpliftFBMPRules3
textcell.paragraph: • Apply the transverse force at the cap reference (or split it equally between these two nodes). Apply the residual moments once. The transverse reaction difference already carries the bearing-level overturning moment.

textcell.name: UpliftFBMPRules4
textcell.paragraph: • Do not also apply C002’s full superstructure cap moment or repeat the vertical wind. Wind on the pier itself remains a separate same-direction load; cap and pier-wall self weight remain in FBMP.

textcell.name: UpliftFBMPRules5
textcell.paragraph: • Physical node IDs and model axis mapping are not supplied. The transfer uses the C002 simple-span horizontal sharing assumption and requires confirmation against the actual bearing restraints and model.

block.paragraph: Residual moments follow the right-hand rule. Reverse T wind to reverse transverse force, roll and yaw; gravity-induced pitch retains its sign. Wind-only increments and equilibrium identities are available in the collapsed derivations.
